children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were higher Wednesday morning, but the increases were beginning to soften, as were the gains in the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed.
Declines in crude oil tempered the upside in the vegetable oils.
The Malaysian palm oil market was closed for a holiday.
The November canola contract remained well above its major moving averages, further underpinning the oilseed.
Statistics Canada projected this year's canola crop at 22.05 million tonnes, down from last year's record production of 22.23 million.
The Manitoba canola harvest reached 36% complete as of Sept. 14, up 21 points on the week.
Canola crush margins edged higher, with the November positions between C$276.90 to C$286.35 per tonne above the futures.
Prairie temperatures were forecast to be in the mid to high teens Celsius Wednesday. Rain is expected for most of the eastern half of the region and clear skies for the western half.
The Canadian dollar stepped back Wednesday morning with the loonie slipping to 71.73 U.S. cents, compared with Tuesday's close of 71.85.
About 26,450 contracts had been traded by 9:59 a.m. ET and prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne were:
